documents.title: Medication check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt. Finished enoxaparin 12/30, no problems. Stopped oxycodone-APAP about a week ago, using plain Tylenol after PT. Has leftover tabs - gave him drop-off info for the police station kiosk. Walking with a cane in the house now. PT 2x/week. Ortho f/u 1/27.

documents.title: Orthopaedic Trauma Clinic - Follow-up
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Orthopaedic trauma clinic, regional hospital. Visit 01/27/2025.

Seen ~8 weeks after fixation of R femoral shaft fracture. Off narcotics. Walking with a cane outdoors, none at home.

Exam: incision well healed. Hip and knee motion functional. NVI.
X-rays: bridging callus forming, hardware unchanged in position.

Plan: full weight bearing, wean cane, continue PT with strengthening. May return to desk/site-office duties; no ladders, no scaffolding, no lifting heavier than light loads until next visit. Return 8 weeks.

Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine - prolonged apnea (pseudocholinesterase deficiency).

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Running low on Creon and the omeprazole. Same pharmacy. Thanks

documents.title: RE: Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Both sent, 90 days with refills. Creon PA is good through October.

conditions.label: Fracture of shaft of right femur, closed

documents.title: Orthopaedic Trauma Clinic - Final Visit
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Orthopaedic trauma clinic, regional hospital. Visit 03/24/2025.

16 weeks out from R femoral shaft ORIF. No pain with walking, no limp. Back at work full time, says he has been careful on ladders.

Exam: full hip and knee range, quad strength now symmetric. Incision healed.
X-rays: fracture united, hardware intact, no loosening.

Assessment: healed right femoral shaft fracture.
Plan: discharged from PT. No restrictions. Hardware stays unless it bothers him. Follow up with us as needed.

Cc: primary care.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Brett is back at full duty since late March, ortho released him. Leg feels normal.

Interval: R femur ORIF 12/2024, healed. Pseudocholinesterase deficiency confirmed (homozygous atypical) after the succinylcholine event - wears the bracelet, showed me. Albumin 3.1 in Dec.

GI: taking enzymes faithfully, stools formed, no abdominal pain, no flares. Eating more protein, mostly shakes at lunch.
CV: no chest pain, no palpitations, no dyspnea on stairs or ladders.

Meds: Creon 36,000 w/ meals + snacks, ASA 81, omeprazole 20.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine - prolonged paralysis (pseudocholinesterase deficiency).
SH: unchanged. Former smoker. Beers on weekends. Back on the motorcycle - we talked about gear.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight unchanged. Well appearing. HEENT normal, dentition fine. Neck no nodes, thyroid normal. Heart regular, apical click and soft late systolic murmur same as before. Lungs clear. Abd obese, soft, nontender. R thigh scar well healed, full strength. No edema. Skin ok.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance - Tdap today. FIT kit given, he will mail it back this week. Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c. PHQ-9 2.
2. Hypoalbuminemia - recheck today.
3. Chronic gallstone pancreatitis - stable on enzymes. Gallbladder still in situ; he wants to get through the building season before thinking about surgery. Revisit in the fall.
4. MVP, mild MR - unchanged exam.
5. Pseudocholinesterase deficiency - documented as high-priority alert.
6. Obesity - stable.

RTC 2 months for a check on albumin and weight.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs look good. Albumin up to 3.4 - still just under normal but heading the right way. Cholesterol and sugar normal, blood counts and liver tests normal. Keep doing what you're doing with the protein.

documents.title: FIT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Repeat in one year. Message sent to patient.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt texted to cancel Monday 7:30. Concrete pour moved up, has to be on site. Will reschedule for the fall, says he feels fine. PCP aware.

documents.title: Fevers
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Doc, been running fevers on and off for about 2 weeks, chills and soaking the sheets some nights. Wiped out by mid afternoon which isn't me. No cough no burning when I pee. Thought it was a summer bug but it's not going away. Had a tooth pulled a few weeks ago if that matters.

documents.title: RE: Fevers
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: It matters, given your valve. I want to see you Friday first thing, 7:30. If you get a fever over 102, shaking chills, chest pain or short of breath before then, go to the ED and text me.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Same-day Visit - Fever
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46M with MVP/mild MR here for ~2 wk of intermittent fevers, night sweats and fatigue. Dental extraction about 3 weeks ago. No cough, dysuria, diarrhea, rash, joint pain, travel. No IV drug use.

Exam: T 38.3, HR 100, otherwise vitals as charted. Tired, not toxic. Mouth: extraction site healed. Heart: there is a new holosystolic blowing murmur at the apex radiating into the axilla, clearly louder and longer than the soft late systolic murmur I have documented before. No rub. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No splinter hemorrhages or conjunctival petechiae that I can see. No edema.

A/P: Fever with a new regurgitant murmur after a dental extraction in a patient with MVP - endocarditis until proven otherwise. He needs blood cultures before any antibiotic and an echo today. Sent directly to the regional hospital ED, called ahead and spoke with the ED physician. No antibiotics given here. He is driving himself - discussed, he insists, it is 10 minutes.

results.text: Positive, 3 of 3 sets: viridans group streptococci. Penicillin MIC 0.06 mcg/mL (susceptible); ceftriaxone susceptible.

reports.text: Indication: fever, new murmur. Normal left ventricular size and systolic function. Mitral valve prolapse. A mobile echodensity consistent with vegetation is attached to the mitral valve. Mild mitral regurgitation. Aortic valve trileaflet, opens normally, no vegetation. Right heart normal. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Vegetation on the mitral valve consistent with infective endocarditis in the setting of mitral valve prolapse.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 08/01/2025.

CC: fevers x2 weeks, new murmur, sent in by PCP.

HPI: 46-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis from gallstones and a prolapsing mitral valve with mild MR, prior right femur ORIF, referred by his primary care physician after two weeks of on-and-off fevers, night sweats and fatigue, with a newly heard murmur. Had a tooth extracted about three weeks ago. No recent travel. Denies intravenous drug use.

PMH: as above; hypoalbuminemia; pseudocholinesterase deficiency.
Meds: pancrelipase with meals and snacks, aspirin 81 mg, omeprazole 20 mg.
Allergies: succinylcholine (prolonged apnea).

Vitals: T 38.5 C, HR 102, BP 130/85.
Exam: dentition in good repair, no dental abscess or gum infection. Cardiac: high-pitched blowing systolic murmur loudest at the apex, radiating to the left axilla. Lungs clear. No peripheral stigmata noted.

Labs: WBC 12.0, Hgb 13.2, Plt 250. ESR 45. Blood cultures x3 drawn before antibiotics.
Formal TTE: vegetation on the mitral valve.

MDM: presumed native mitral valve endocarditis after dental extraction. Cardiology and ID notified. Ceftriaxone 2 g IV given after cultures.
Disposition: admitted to medicine.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Medicine
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, medicine service
Admitted 08/01/2025, discharged 08/07/2025

Principal diagnosis: native mitral valve infective endocarditis, viridans group streptococci, following dental extraction.
Other: mitral valve prolapse with mild MR; chronic gallstone pancreatitis on enzymes; hypoalbuminemia; obesity; pseudocholinesterase deficiency.

Course: Admitted from ED with fever and a new apical murmur; TTE showed a mitral valve vegetation. All three admission blood culture sets grew viridans group streptococci, penicillin MIC 0.06. Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h continued from the ED. Defervesced on hospital day 2. Surveillance cultures 08/03 no growth. Infectious disease and cardiology consulted; TEE not pursued given a diagnostic TTE and no clinical sign of perivalvular extension; no surgical indication identified. Dental evaluation found good oral hygiene with no ongoing source. Albumin 2.8 on 08/02. PICC placed 08/05 (right basilic) without complication.

Discharge plan: ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 24 hours through 08/28/2025 via home infusion; weekly CBC and BMP to ID clinic; ID clinic visit in about 2 weeks; repeat TTE at end of therapy with cardiology; PCP within one week.
Home medications unchanged: pancrelipase, aspirin 81 mg, omeprazole 20 mg.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine (pseudocholinesterase deficiency).

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home since yesterday. Home infusion nurse came this morning, ceftriaxone running fine through PICC, he's been taught to flush. No fever since the hospital. Tired. PICC site clean, no arm swelling. Labs will be drawn Mondays by the infusion nurse. TCM visit Tue 8/12 confirmed. Work note requested - off through the end of antibiotics, PCP to sign.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit after admission 8/1-8/7 for viridans strep mitral valve endocarditis (3/3 cultures, PCN MIC 0.06), sent in from here the day he presented. Repeat cultures 8/3 no growth. On ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily via R arm PICC through 8/28. ID following; echo again at end of therapy.

Feels better each day, sleeping through without sweats. Appetite coming back. Down about 3.5 kg from his usual. No fevers at home. No chest pain or breathlessness.

Meds: ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h (home infusion), Creon w/ meals and snacks, ASA 81, omeprazole 20.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Looks less washed out. Heart regular, holosystolic apical murmur radiating to axilla, unchanged from 8/1. Lungs clear. PICC R upper arm clean, no tenderness, no arm swelling. No edema.

Labs 8/11 from home infusion: WBC now normal, renal function and potassium normal.

A/P:
1. Mitral valve IE on ceftriaxone - responding. Complete course 8/28. Weekly labs. ID f/u.
2. Hypoalbuminemia - 2.8 inpatient; will recheck after antibiotics are done.
3. Weight loss from the illness - expect it to come back.
4. Work - off through end of therapy, note signed.
5. Will talk about dental prophylaxis going forward once he is off IV antibiotics.

documents.title: Infectious Disease Clinic Note
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Infectious disease clinic, regional hospital. Visit 08/21/2025.

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for following Mr. Coughlin with us. He is on day 21 of ceftriaxone for native mitral valve endocarditis due to viridans group streptococci (PCN MIC 0.06), after a dental extraction. Cultures cleared by 08/03.

He is afebrile and feels close to normal. No rash, no diarrhea. PICC site clean. Weekly labs reviewed and unremarkable.

Exam: well appearing. Apical systolic murmur radiating to the axilla. No embolic phenomena. No PICC site erythema.

Plan: complete ceftriaxone 2 g daily through 08/28/2025, then home infusion will pull the PICC after the final dose. End-of-therapy TTE with cardiology. He now meets criteria for antibiotic prophylaxis before dental procedures that manipulate gingiva, given prior endocarditis; we would suggest amoxicillin 2 g orally 30-60 minutes beforehand. No routine follow-up needed with us unless fever recurs.

Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine (pseudocholinesterase deficiency).

documents.title: Line out
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Last bag was the 28th, nurse pulled the PICC yesterday. Arm's fine. Can I go back to work Monday? Need a note for the company.

documents.title: RE: Line out
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news. Yes, back Monday, full duty. Note attached. Take it a little easy the first week - your stamina will lag behind how you feel. Echo with cardiology is coming up in October.

medications.sig: Take 4 capsules (2 g) by mouth 30-60 minutes before dental procedures

documents.title: Dentist
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Dentist wants to see me for a cleaning and says I need antibiotics first now? Is that right

documents.title: RE: Dentist
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, that's right now that you've had endocarditis. Before any dental work, including cleanings, take 4 amoxicillin capsules (2 grams total) 30 to 60 minutes before the appointment. I've sent a prescription to your pharmacy with refills so you always have a dose at home. Let the dentist know about the bracelet too, in case they ever sedate you.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u. Finished 4 wk ceftriaxone 8/28 for mitral valve IE, PICC out 9/2. Back to full duty 9/8. Energy most of the way back. No fevers, no sweats. Had his dental cleaning with amoxicillin beforehand, no issues.

GI: enzymes with meals, no pain, stools ok.

Meds: Creon 36,000 w/ meals + snacks, ASA 81, omeprazole 20, amoxicillin 2 g before dental work.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Heart regular, apical systolic murmur radiating to the axilla, same as August. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. Old PICC site healed. No edema.

A/P:
1. Mitral valve IE, treated - TTE with cardiology 10/20.
2. Hypoalbuminemia - recheck today.
3. Chronic gallstone pancreatitis - stable. Raised cholecystectomy again; he would rather do it in winter when work slows. Will plan referral in January.
4. Flu shot today.
5. Covid booster - will get at pharmacy.

RTC January.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Counts normal, kidney and liver normal. Albumin 3.1 - dipped with the infection, as expected. We'll keep an eye on it in January.

documents.title: Pancrelipase prior authorization renewal
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Creon 36,000 PA expiring. Renewal submitted with last office note and dx. Approved through 10/2026. Pharmacy notified.

reports.text: Indication: completed therapy for mitral valve endocarditis. Normal left ventricular size and systolic function. Mitral valve prolapse; no residual vegetation. Mild mitral regurgitation. Aortic valve normal. Normal right ventricle. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: No residual vegetation. Mitral valve prolapse with mild mitral regurgitation. Normal LV size and function.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Visit 10/20/2025.

Dear Doctor,

I saw Mr. Coughlin, 46, after treatment of native mitral valve endocarditis (viridans streptococci, 4 weeks ceftriaxone ending 08/28/2025), on a background of mitral valve prolapse with mild regurgitation. His father has MVP as well.

He feels well. No dyspnea, orthopnea, palpitations or exertional limitation; back to supervising job sites.

Exam: BP and HR normal. Mid-systolic click with an apical systolic murmur radiating to the axilla. Lungs clear. No edema.

Echo today: no residual vegetation; prolapse with mild MR; normal LV size and function.

Impression: endocarditis resolved. MVP with mild MR.
Recommendations: continue amoxicillin prophylaxis before dental procedures for life. Repeat echo in 2-3 years or sooner with symptoms. No restrictions. Return as needed.

Medications reviewed: pancrelipase, aspirin 81 mg, omeprazole 20 mg, amoxicillin pre-dental.
Allergies/alerts: succinylcholine.
